text:
A: Hiya! Can you hear me okay?
B: Yeah, loud and clear. Hiya, I'm Yusuf. Gemma, is it?
A: That's me, yeah. Nice to meet you. How are you doing?
B: Not bad, not bad. Bit knackered, I went gym before this, which was a mistake, my legs are gone. How about you?
A: Oh I'm alright, thanks. I've just got through a pile of maths books at the kitchen table, so I'm feeling quite smug actually.
B: Maths books. Teacher, then?
A: Yeah, primary. Year 4 in Wigan. And I'm maths lead as well, which sounds dead fancy but mostly it means I get the emails nobody else wants.
B: Ha, I know that feeling, mate. Erm, so I'm an exec assistant, I work for two directors at a property consultancy in Birmingham. Basically I keep two grown men's diaries alive. Client lunches, travel, board minutes, all that. If I'm off sick for a day, honestly, the whole place just stops. I'm not even joking.
A: So it's like having two Year 4s then.
B: Do you know what, Year 4s are probably better behaved. At least yours can tell the time.
A: You'd be surprised. We're doing analogue clocks at the minute and it's carnage.
B: Carnage, I bet. So did you do that puzzle thing at the start? How'd you get on?
A: Erm, alright I think? I did the first bit really quick and then just sort of stared at the last one for ages. You?
B: Same, same. I reckon I got most of them. I'm saying most. Couldn't swear to it.
A: That's the spirit.
B: Is that a Warriors magnet on your fridge? I can see it behind you.
A: Oh, it is, yeah! Well spotted. My family are Wigan Warriors through and through, my dad's been taking me since I was little and now I take our Lily as well, she's eleven. We go to a few home games a season and watch the Grand Final at my mum and dad's. Do you follow rugby at all?
B: Not really, I'm football. Villa, all day. I get to a few home games when a client's got a spare hospitality seat, which, I'm not gonna lie, is the best way to watch it. Free food.
A: Free food is always the best way to do anything.
B: Exactly. Exactly that. You got any holidays sorted this year?
A: Tenerife, same place as last year. I always go back to the same resort with Lily and sometimes my mum. All-inclusive, kids' club, done. I need to book it before the prices go up, actually, you've reminded me.
B: See, I couldn't do the same place twice. I always want somewhere new. Last year was Marrakech with my girlfriend, before that Dubai. I like a nice hotel, bit beyond my budget, if I'm honest.
A: I'd find all that a bit stressful, to be fair. The planning and that. I like knowing where the pool is and where they do the chips.
B: No, that's fair, that's fair. Different strokes.
A: And to be honest, with an eleven-year-old you just want an easy life. She's starting high school in September and the uniform alone has cost me a fortune.
B: Oh, the blazer and everything? My mum used to moan about that with all four of us.
A: The blazer, the PE kit, the special socks with the logo on. Socks! I said to the lady, they're socks.
B: Mate, they got you. That's a racket, that.
A: It is. Anyway, my treat to myself is a pie barm on a Friday from the bakery, so that keeps me going.
B: A pie barm? Sorry, what's a barm?
A: A bread roll! A barm cake. Pie inside a barm. Don't look at me like that.
B: A pie in a bap? That's mad. That's carbs in carbs.
A: It's a Wigan thing, it's beautiful, you'd love it.
